judgment.rationale: The author says Keyboard Manager shortcuts stop working after some time while single-key remaps continue, but gives no shortcut, trigger sequence, or affected application. Public replies mention unrelated possible causes without author confirmation. The smallest useful next step is to identify one failing mapping and whether restarting or locking the session changes it.
evidence: The issue body says shortcuts worked initially and later failed, while key remaps remained functional; the author says they cannot reproduce a clear trigger.
A commenter suggests a Peek key/keyboard rollover possibility, and another suggests a WeChat session/lock-screen workaround linked to #25032; neither is confirmed by the reporter.
The report identifies PowerToys 0.96.1 but does not list a failing shortcut or keyboard layout.
judgment.recommended_action: Request one exact failing shortcut, its target, the affected application, and whether locking/unlocking the session restores it.

fix_assessment.rationale: The report is not yet scoped enough to identify a PowerToys code path or a testable fix hypothesis.

issue_context.summary: The author reports intermittent Keyboard Manager shortcut failures after initially successful use, while single-key mappings continue to work.
known_information: The report lists PowerToys 0.96.1 and Keyboard Manager.
The author says shortcuts fail without an obvious trigger and restarting the program did not help.
The issue has three comments: one notes a missing conflict warning, one suggests a Peek/keyboard-rollover possibility, and one suggests a WeChat session/lock workaround.
The live issue has no assignee and no attachment.
inferences: A stale or conflicting shortcut registration is possible, but the discussion does not distinguish it from a device rollover or another application's interception.
The WeChat suggestion is unconfirmed and must not be treated as the cause.
issue_context.analysis: A specific failing mapping and the state transition that restores it would materially narrow the engine path. Repeating a generic diagnostics request would not resolve the missing reproduction.
initial_investigation: Read the full issue body and all three comments; the suggested fixes come from commenters and have not been confirmed by the author.
Checked current Keyboard Manager engine/editor ownership; without the chord, target, and affected application there is no defensible code-level hypothesis.

information_gaps.information: One exact source shortcut, its configured target, the affected application, and numbered steps from a fresh PowerToys start until it stops working.
information_gaps.why_needed: This separates a mapping-specific engine failure from a conflict or application-specific interception.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Please list the keys exactly as shown in Keyboard Manager, the target, and the steps that cause the first failure.

information_gaps.information: Whether locking and unlocking Windows or signing out and back in restores that same shortcut.
information_gaps.why_needed: A session transition can distinguish persistent configuration problems from a lost runtime registration or external hook.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: After the same shortcut fails, test Win+L/unlock once and report whether it works again.

information_gaps.information: The keyboard language/layout and any keyboard remapping software involved.
information_gaps.why_needed: Layout or another remapper can change the physical-to-logical chord and compete with Keyboard Manager.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Please name the active Windows keyboard layout and any running remapper; do not include unrelated system details.

comment.body:
Thanks for noting that the shortcut mappings stop working while single-key remaps continue, and that restarting PowerToys did not restore them. The replies mention possible Peek/keyboard-rollover or WeChat session behavior, but the issue does not identify which shortcut fails, so we cannot tell whether those explanations apply. Please provide:
- One exact source shortcut and target as shown in Keyboard Manager, the affected application, and short steps from a fresh PowerToys start until the first failure.
- Whether Win+L and unlocking restores that same shortcut after it fails.
- The active keyboard layout or other remapper if one is running.
This will distinguish a mapping-specific failure from session-state or input interception.
